comments.body: Filed as story B of the compact-on-close split (operator direction 2026-08-12). Story A is choosy-arthrodic-barbet — it removes inline compact-on-close and lands the P0 lock fix on its own; this ticket restores an automatic compaction trigger out of band. depends_on A because A removes the standing trigger this ticket replaces, and because review-plan on a ticket still blocked by an unclosed prerequisite fast-fails without running the LLM — so this plan gets its review after A closes.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implemented. Plan PASSED on the third review — the two earlier BLOCKs were both correct and both changed the design, so recording them:

1. (T9/E2, T3) The first draft invented a 'dedicated clone' concept and left its lifecycle and signing bootstrap unspecified. Fixed by grounding it in the EXISTING precedent instead: .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml already runs a scheduled job that writes ticket events and pushes them, from an ephemeral runner. Its store-mount recipe (fetch '+tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets', rm -rf .tickets-tracker, git worktree add -B tickets .tickets-tracker origin/tickets), its bot git identity, and its 0600 REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY materialization are all reused. Also learned that env identity needs NO bootstrap at all: _seam.env_id reads <tracker>/.env-id, which is CONTENT of the tickets branch, so a worktree of origin/tickets carries the store's own env id automatically.

2. (G6) The second draft would have CHURNED. I proposed selecting tickets by raw live event count, but the fold only squashes events older than the compaction horizon (is_foldable, 30 min default). A ticket over threshold whose excess events were all young would be selected, fold nothing, be counted as compacted, and be selected again forever. Fixed by having selection reuse the fold's OWN predicate against the same horizon, so the two cannot drift.

3. (G6 again) My first attempt at the honest-reporting guard had no mechanism: _compact_locked returns 0 for a successful fold AND for all three no-op branches, so the driver could not tell them apart from the return code. Rather than change the return contract (which every compact_cli caller inherits), the driver now observes the ARTIFACT — the set of *-SNAPSHOT.json names before and after — and counts a ticket compacted only when a new one appeared.

Biggest implementation finding: I did NOT need a new sweep module. compact-all already existed and already did the enumerate/limit/dry-run/fold/batch-commit/push work. Its only defect was SELECTION — _scan_snapshot_state returned only tickets LACKING a SNAPSHOT, making it a one-time backfill that could never re-fold a grown ticket. So this is a ~50-line widening of an existing verb plus a workflow, not a new engine.

Changes: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py (foldable-count selection + honest counting), .github/workflows/compact-sweep.yml (new, 6-hourly, workflow_dispatch with dry_run/limit), docs/concurrency.md (I9b now names the concrete trigger and cadence), tests/unit/test_compact_all_selection.py (6 tests), tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_sweep_races.py (3 tests).

RED verified: restoring the old selection and the old rc==0 counting fails 4 of the 6 selection tests. actionlint and zizmor both clean on the new workflow (needed hash-pinned actions and persist-credentials: true, matching the reconciler). Gates green: 13 check_*.py, complexity baseline unchanged, lint, mypy (519 files), all five generators with zero diff. Full pytest and the integration tier are running now — and this time I am running the integration tier explicitly, since CI's main invocation excludes it and that is exactly where change 1702's only CI failure surfaced.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Caught and fixed a real regression I had introduced — worth recording because I had ALREADY talked myself past it.

The integration tier failed tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py::test_compact_all_limit_compacts_only_n. That test seeds four fresh tickets (one CREATE event each) and expects compact-all to backfill them. My implementation selected purely on 'foldable count > threshold', and 1 is not > 10, so compact-all silently STOPPED backfilling small tickets. A one-line behaviour change to an existing documented contract, invisible in the unit tier because every fixture I wrote happened to be over threshold.

What makes this worth writing down: my own approved plan said 'a widening, not a replacement' and 'backfill becomes the special case where the whole log is foldable'. That second clause was simply wrong — a 1-event ticket's whole log IS foldable, but 1 is not greater than 10, so the threshold arm does not cover the backfill case. The plan reviewer had pushed me twice on selection semantics and I still got this wrong in the direction the plan itself warned against. The test caught what my reasoning did not.

Fix: selection is now explicitly TWO ARMS, either of which selects —
  1. Backfill (historical, preserved): no SNAPSHOT and at least one foldable event.
  2. Recurrence (new): foldable count > compact.threshold, whatever the snapshot state.
Arm 2 alone regresses backfill; arm 1 alone is the one-time-only bug this story exists to fix. Both converge: after a fold the ticket has a SNAPSHOT and its live count is back under threshold, so neither arm re-selects it.

Added two tests for the arm I broke — a small snapshot-less ticket is still backfilled, and the backfill arm converges on the next sweep — and corrected test_under_threshold_ticket_is_not_selected, which had been passing for the wrong reason (it asserted a snapshot-LESS ticket was skipped, which was only true because of the bug). Also corrected docs/concurrency.md I9b, which described only the threshold rule.

Process note for myself: CI's main pytest invocation excludes the integration tier (-m 'not integration'), and this is the SECOND time in this session that the only real failure lived exactly there — change 1702's s3_doctor flake was the first. Running tests/integration explicitly is not optional here.

Gates re-run clean after the fix: lint, mypy (519 files), complexity baseline unchanged, wall-clock-assert, comment-hygiene, docs-index. Both full tiers re-running now.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Two MORE failures from the full tier, both mine, both fixed. Recording because the third one was a genuine design trap I would not have found by reasoning.

2. tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py::test_every_workflow_is_named_in_the_locked_table — the repo locks every workflow filename to an exact display name, and a new workflow with no entry fails until it is named deliberately. Registered compact-sweep.yml -> 'Compaction Sweep'. Working exactly as intended; nothing to argue with.

3. tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py::test_compact_all_keeps_the_legacy_best_effort_push_contract — this one is the interesting one. It asserts compact-all always triggers push_after_commit. It broke because of my HONEST COUNTING change, not my selection change, and the coupling was invisible:

  - The old code counted every rc==0 as compacted, including folds that wrote nothing. So 'compacted > 0' really meant 'we selected something', and the commit+push tail behind it effectively always ran.
  - Once counting became honest, a sweep that folds nothing has compacted == 0, so the tail — and with it the push — was silently skipped.

That is a real regression in a contract that has nothing to do with counting: the push exists so an earlier unpushed write in the same session is not stranded, and a sweep is often the last thing to run. Whether THIS sweep folded anything is irrelevant to it.

Fixed by decoupling them. A best-effort push now runs on every non-dry-run invocation that commits nothing — including the 'Nothing to do' early return, which previously could not push at all — while the commit+push tail still runs when something was actually folded. --no-commit still opts out of both, as before.

Note this test also exposed why I keep the backfill arm's 'at least one foldable event' condition: its fixture ticket is freshly created, so every event is inside the 30-minute horizon and nothing is foldable yet. The sweep correctly does nothing and correctly still pushes. The next scheduled run, 6 hours later, sees aged events and folds them.

Tally for this story: the full tier caught 3 failures, all mine, none of which the unit tier or my own reasoning caught — a selection regression, a config-lock omission, and a coupling between an honest-counting change and an unrelated push contract. Re-running both tiers now with all three fixed; gates already re-verified clean (lint, mypy 519 files, complexity baseline unchanged, generators zero diff).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Change 1717 got LLM-Review +1 with 5 advisory (non-blocking) findings. I fixed all 5 rather than landing on the +1 — two were real defects and one was a test of mine that overclaimed.

1. (correctness) REAL BUG: 'compact-all --dry-run performs a real push when nothing is selected'. I put _best_effort_push on the total_needs == 0 early return, BEFORE the dry_run guard, and it only checked no_commit. So a dry run with nothing selected delivered whatever was pending. A dry run must have no side effects, and pushing is a side effect even when this invocation committed nothing of its own. _best_effort_push now takes keyword-only no_commit and dry_run and opts out of both. Added tests for --dry-run and --no-commit never pushing.

2. (tests) REAL, and the finding I am most glad of: test_two_independent_folds_of_one_ticket_converge never MERGED the two clones. It folded in both and asserted each still reduced correctly — which proves nothing about the race its own docstring claimed to test. Two sweeps racing are on different machines and never see each other's locks, so convergence is a property of the union merge (I9), not of exclusion. A test that skips the merge tests nothing.
   Rewrote it to actually fetch and merge clone B into clone A, and ran the experiment first to learn the real behaviour rather than assume it: each fold writes a SNAPSHOT under its own unique filename and renames the SAME sources to *.retired; git merges the identical renames as one change and both snapshots as adds; the merge is CLEAN (ort) and the ticket ends up carrying TWO snapshots, which the reducer tolerates and replays to identical state. The test now asserts exactly that — clean merge, both snapshots present, retired sources intact, same comment set.

3. (tests) The new best-effort push path was untested — which is pointed, because that path exists precisely because I broke it invisibly. Added a test that a sweep folding nothing still pushes, and one that the 'Nothing to do' early return still pushes.

4. (error-handling) My _best_effort_push docstring claimed pure best-effort, but push_after_commit deliberately re-raises OptionalDependencyError so a misconfigured S3 remote halts loudly. Corrected the docstring to state the fail-closed escape and why it is preserved: silencing it would make the one unrecoverable configuration error invisible on the store's only standing trigger.

5. (iac) The workflow declared no timeout-minutes, inheriting GitHub's 6-hour default while reconcile-bridge.yml and _build-and-test.yml both bound at 60. Added timeout-minutes: 60 with the rationale that a truncated sweep is harmless — compaction is optional and the next run re-folds what is pending.

Gates re-verified: lint (needed a ruff format pass on the rewritten test), mypy 523 files, complexity baseline, wall-clock-assert, actionlint + zizmor clean. 57 tests across the affected modules pass. Amended onto the same Change-Id; full tiers re-running before I re-push.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Pushed patch set 2 of change 1717 (commit 4fbbda329f) with all 5 review findings fixed.

Triaged the ps1 Verified -1 before pushing, per the playbook. Failure was tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py::test_pass_summary_reports_the_decline_count on ONE shard (macos-latest py3.13); ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 passed the identical code. It is NOT mine and NOT covered by my amendment — category (b), a known order-dependent test with a fix in flight.

Evidence, in the order I got it:
- My diff touches compact.py, compact-sweep.yml, docs/concurrency.md and compaction/workflow tests. Nothing reaches the reconciler.
- The test passes in ISOLATION on macOS, the same platform that failed: 10/10.
- Running the whole tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ directory alone passes too (3 random orderings). So the trigger is cross-directory state, not anything within that suite.
- My own full main tier reproduced it (1 failed, 12715 passed) — so I could study it locally rather than argue from CI logs.
- DECISIVE: git log on that test file returns exactly one commit, 4010da6493 'Decline removals of never-confirmed peer links', dated 2026-08-12 — one of the 8 commits I rebased onto. The file is brand new. It cannot have been broken by a change that post-dates it, and my earlier pre-rebase full run (12665 passed, 0 failed) did not contain it at all.

Mechanism, for whoever holds the in-flight fix: the test asserts a once-per-pass INFO summary ('declined N inbound link removal(s)', apply_inbound_records.py:792) reaches caplog. The captured records contain the PER-LINK decline message from the same module logger, so logger propagation is intact — the summary simply was not emitted, which points at the  counter rather than at log capture. Adding tests elsewhere in the suite reshuffles pytest-randomly's ordering, which is why an unrelated change surfaces it.

I did NOT recheck this one, because a recheck re-runs the same order-dependent test and the fix is already in flight; ps2 gets a fresh CI run anyway, and if it trips again the answer is that fix landing, not a retry from me.

Local state on ps2: main tier 12715 passed with only that known flake failing; integration tier 194 passed, 1 skipped; gates all green. Waiting on ps2 votes.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Correction to the previous comment: one word was lost to shell backtick substitution when I
posted it. The sentence should read "...which points at the `declined` counter rather than at
log capture" — the identifier is `declined`, the local counter in
`apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` that guards the once-per-pass summary at
`apply_inbound_records.py:788` (`if declined:`). Nothing else in that comment was affected.

My own process note: I passed that comment body as a double-quoted shell argument, so every
backticked identifier in it was executed as a command substitution. Any backtick-quoted symbol
name in a `rebar comment` written that way is silently replaced by the output of running it —
usually empty. Comment bodies with code identifiers go through a heredoc or a file from here
on, which is how this one was written.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OPERATOR DESIGN CONSTRAINT (verbatim):

"compaction needs to work in environments without local cron and CI. that's why the original
design was linked to an operation."

This is a real gap in what I have built, and I did not see it. Story A removed the
operation-linked trigger (compact-on-close) and change 1717 replaces it with a GitHub Actions
schedule — which is OUR repo's infrastructure. An adopter running rebar as a library or CLI
with no CI and no local cron now has NO compaction trigger at all: their event logs would grow
without bound, and nothing in the product would ever fold them. I optimised for this repo and
called it "the store's only standing trigger" without asking what a store outside this repo
would do.

The scheduled sweep is still right as the amortized path where CI exists. What is missing is a
FLOOR that works everywhere: an operation-linked trigger that does not reintroduce the 13m53s
lock hold story A removed.

Required shape (operator-specified design space):
- after a covered write completes and RELEASES the store lock (close being the natural
  candidate), check the two-arm selection cheaply;
- if work exists, run the fold out-of-band from the session's perspective — either a detached
  local worker, or inline but with fold-outside-lock discipline: fold with NO lock held, then
  take the lock only for the rename+commit, with a re-check.

Operational nuance to respect: the detached-worker pattern already exists in this codebase as
`enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain`. Reuse its shape — including the stamped-lock discipline
just fixed in change 1704 — rather than inventing a third dialect.

The ticket must NOT close with the CI-less gap open.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DECISION: land 1717 as-is, then an immediate STACKED follow-up change on this ticket for the
operation-linked fallback. The ticket stays open until both land.

Why not a new patchset on 1717: the two mechanisms are genuinely separable — 1717 is the
amortized CI path, the fallback is the everywhere-floor — and they have different blast
radii and different tests. Folding them together would produce one change that touches a
workflow, the sweep selection, the close path and a new detached worker, reviewed as a lump.
1717 ps2 is also mid-CI right now; amending discards that run for no reviewer benefit. Stacked
keeps both units reviewable, which is what CONTRIBUTING asks for.

DESIGN (to be reviewed through the plan gate before I write it):

Trigger, on the close path where `_compact_on_close` used to sit — but AFTER the store lock is
released and after the best-effort push, so nothing the session waits on holds the lock. Two
O(1) checks, either of which fires:
  - the ticket just written satisfies the two-arm selection (one listdir + parse of that
    ticket's own events — independent of store size); or
  - a last-sweep stamp file is older than a configured interval (one stat). This second check
    is what makes the floor real: without it, a store whose closed tickets happen not to need
    folding would never fold the ones that do.

Execution: spawn a DETACHED worker that runs the full `compact-all` sweep, reusing
`enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain`'s shape verbatim — the PYTHONPATH bootstrap for the bare
python child, `_detach_kwargs()` (start_new_session/close_fds on POSIX, DETACHED_PROCESS on
Windows), stdio to DEVNULL and a log file. The session returns immediately; the fold happens
with the same lock profile as a manual `rebar compact`, which is the accepted baseline, and
never across an LLM call.

Storm control: a stamped advisory lock beside the drain lock in `.rebar/`, using the SAME v2
ownership stamp and the SAME shared decision table `lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale` that
change 1704 just fixed for the drain lock — so pid-recycle qualification, refusal-without-proof
and the wall-clock ceiling are inherited, not re-invented. One compactor at a time; a caller
that finds the lock held simply does not spawn.

Windows is a v1 no-op, mirroring the drain, because the store lock's fcntl import would crash a
detached child there.

A tri-state config knob mirroring `overlap_drain` (async detaches / always runs inline for
tests and CI / off), so the suite can exercise the fold synchronously and an operator can
disable it.

This does NOT reintroduce the P0: the P0 was that an operation an agent WAITS ON held the lock
for 13m53s. Here the waiting operation holds nothing, and the worker's hold is bounded by the
same fold the scheduled sweep performs.

Note this changes ticket material, and the completion-verification close gate checks
plan-review validity for a story, so the description gets this design and a fresh passing
review before anything lands.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Change 1717 ps2: LLM-Review +1 again, with 5 NEW advisories. Fixed all 5 — two were real
correctness bugs in code I had just written, and one was a false claim in my own docs.

1. (correctness) `_foldable_event_count` counted forward-compat UNKNOWN-TYPE events as
   foldable, but the fold drops them: `_parse_candidate_events` skips any event whose
   `event_type` is not in `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`, preserving a newer clone's event kind untouched
   rather than squashing it. So selection promised work the fold would never do, and a ticket
   whose excess was all unknown-type would be selected on every single sweep forever — the
   exact churn class the earlier review round made me fix, reintroduced through a different
   door. Selection now mirrors the fold's filter.

2. (correctness) `_foldable_event_count` counted the ticket's OWN `-SNAPSHOT.json` toward the
   foldable total: SNAPSHOT is a KNOWN_EVENT_TYPE and its filename ends in `.json`, so nothing
   excluded it. Every settled ticket therefore reported one unit of outstanding work forever —
   a permanent off-by-one that becomes a churn source at low thresholds. A snapshot is
   already-folded STATE, not pending work; it is excluded now. Both fixes have regression tests.

3. (docs) I claimed in `docs/concurrency.md` and in the workflow header that the sweep runs in
   a clone with "its own `.git`, its own index". That is wrong: the workflow mounts the store
   with `git worktree add`, and a worktree SHARES the checkout's object store. The isolation
   that actually matters is that the runner is a separate checkout on a separate machine, so
   it shares no `index.lock`, no `rebar-git-op.lock` and no store write lock with an
   interactive session. Corrected in both places rather than left as a plausible-sounding
   overstatement.

4. (iac) The sweep had no failure notification or telemetry, unlike the reconcile-bridge
   template it copies. Compaction is invisible when it works and equally invisible when it
   silently stops, so a store whose sweep has quietly folded nothing for weeks looks healthy.
   Added a step-summary report of the sweep's counts on every run and a failure notification
   mirroring the bridge's. Its text also states the honest severity: events stay live and
   valid, and a CI-less store still compacts via the operation-linked trigger, so a failed
   sweep degrades cadence, not correctness.

5. (tests) The exit-2 path was untested even though the workflow BRANCHES on it (warn and
   pass) versus any other non-zero (fail). Added tests that a per-ticket fold failure yields
   exit 2, that it does not stop the sweep folding the other tickets, and that a clean sweep is
   exit 0.

Also fixed while wiring the operation-linked trigger: adding its call to `close_ticket` pushed
that function from 17 to 18 complexity, and `.github/complexity-baseline.json` is a shrink-only
ratchet. Rather than raise the ceiling I extracted `_trigger_compaction` as a guard function so
the call site stays unconditional — the same pattern, and the same stated reason, as
`_ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked` in `close_precheck`.

ps2's Verified -1 was the SAME known order-dependent reconciler test on the same macOS shard
(`test_pass_summary_reports_the_decline_count`), already triaged: introduced by 4010da6493
yesterday, fix in flight, not reachable from this diff. I did not recheck it for the same
reason as last time.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
The full main tier caught a REAL defect in the operation-linked trigger — and this one was mine
by design, not by accident: 12 failed + 5 errors, scattered across unrelated interface tests,
all "git commit failed" / "git operation failed".

Cause: `compact.trigger` defaults to `async`, so every close in the suite spawned a DETACHED
compaction worker against that test's temp store. The children outlived the tests that spawned
them and raced the NEXT test's writes for the store lock and the git-op lock. The workers were
doing legitimate work; it simply was not that process's work.

Two fixes, because there are two distinct problems and only one of them is about tests.

1. PRODUCTION — the worker now STANDS ASIDE when a foreground writer holds the store lock.
   Compaction is optional housekeeping and must yield to work someone is waiting on, never
   compete with it. What is satisfying here: this is the bug-7084 probe, the one I proved
   USELESS earlier in this very investigation. Inline on the close path it could never fire,
   because the closing process had released the lock microseconds before its own probe, so the
   store always read "free" — that was a key part of the root-cause argument for the original
   P0. Out of band the same probe measures something real: another SESSION's activity, because
   the compactor is now a different process from every writer it might obstruct. Moving the
   work is what made the guard meaningful. Racy and fail-open by design — a skipped sweep is a
   no-op for correctness, so guessing wrong in either direction costs nothing.

2. TEST HYGIENE — an autouse conftest fixture defaults `REBAR_COMPACT_TRIGGER=off` for the
   offline suite, in the same shape as the existing network and repo-commit guards: the ambient
   default is the safe one, and a test that exercises the trigger opts in explicitly. A unit
   suite must not have background writers. `tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py` opts back in to
   `async` for itself.

Note the fixture-ordering trap I walked into on the way: my module-level opt-in was written as
"set async if unset", which never fired, because the conftest fixture had already put `off` in
the environment. Fixed to set it unconditionally; a test wanting another mode calls setenv in
its own body, which runs after every fixture and wins.

Added a stand-aside test AND its positive control (same setup, lock not held, fold happens) —
without the control the stand-aside test would pass even if the sweep were broken outright.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
The rebased main tier caught two more of mine. Both fixed; both worth recording because one is
a repeat of a mistake I had already made and named in this same ticket.

1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` hit 808 LOC, over the 800 hard cap — my CompactConfig comment
   block pushed it past. The cap is absolute and deliberately has no allowlist. Fixed by
   compressing the schema comments to four lines that point at where the rationale already
   lives (`compact_trigger`'s module docstring and `docs/config.md`), which is the better home
   for it anyway — the schema should say WHAT the key is, not argue the design. 799 now.

2. `test_the_close_holds_no_store_lock_across_the_trigger` failed, and the TEST was wrong, not
   the code. I wrote it with `trigger=always` and the comment "worst case: fold inline, not
   detached". That reasoning is backwards: `always` exists precisely to run the fold INLINE so
   the suite can observe it, so of course the folding process holds the store lock while it
   folds. I asserted a production property against a test-only mode, and it proved nothing —
   it only started failing once the trigger actually began firing in that test.

   Rewritten to exercise `async`, the production mode, with the spawn stubbed: the close must
   write NO fold artifact and never be seen holding the lock while one exists, and it must have
   DELEGATED (the spawn recorded). That is the property that matters.

   This is the second test in this ticket that overclaimed — the first was the convergence test
   that never merged, caught by the code reviewer. Same root error both times: I wrote the
   assertion I wanted to be true rather than the one the setup could actually establish. Worth
   naming rather than quietly fixing.

Also: a 101-char line tripped E501 and the pre-commit hook correctly refused the amend, which
is the gate doing its job — I nearly recorded a "committed" state that had not committed.

Gates green after both fixes: ruff clean, mypy 526 files, complexity ratchet unchanged,
module-size contract passing. Re-running the full main tier on the fixed stack before pushing.

comments.body:

  amortized path where CI exists.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Change 1727 got LLM-Review +1 with 5 advisories. I read them before CI finished rather than
waiting, because on 1717 the advisories caught two real bugs both times. Same again: one of
these was a hole straight through the floor this change exists to be.

1. (correctness) THE IMPORTANT ONE. `run_sweep` stamped the last-sweep clock in its `finally`
   — including when it had just STOOD ASIDE because the store lock was busy. A stand-aside
   folds nothing, so stamping it resets the staleness arm for a full interval. Under sustained
   contention every trigger would stand aside, stamp, and go quiet: the store would never
   compact while LOOKING freshly swept. That is worse than having no floor, because the signal
   says it is working.

   What makes this worth dwelling on: I introduced it while fixing a different review finding.
   Stamping in a `finally` reads as tidy bookkeeping, and the guard I had just added (stand
   aside when busy) is exactly what turned tidy bookkeeping into a silent failure mode. Fixed
   by deleting the stamp from `run_sweep` entirely — `compact_all_cli` already stamps when it
   actually sweeps, and that is the only event the stamp may record. Which also resolved
   advisory 4 (the stamp was being written twice per successful sweep). Added a test that a
   stand-aside leaves the clock alone AND that the next trigger therefore still fires.

2. (iac) `| tee` under `set -o pipefail` made the captured `rc` the pipeline's rightmost
   non-zero exit, so a `tee` failure (unwritable RUNNER_TEMP, full disk) would masquerade as
   rebar's exit code — defeating the exit-2-vs-1 branching I had just added tests for two
   rounds ago. Replaced the pipe with a redirect plus `cat`.

3. (tests) The dry-run stamp guard was untested. Added: a dry run leaves the clock unset, a
   real sweep sets it.

4. (maintainability) Double `record_sweep` — resolved by fix 1.

5. (maintainability) My own explanatory comment in `close_ticket` still said "Compaction is NOT
   run here" and described the trigger as "an out-of-band sweep that runs in a DEDICATED
   CLONE". Both stale: the close DOES trigger compaction now (it just delegates), and I had
   already corrected the dedicated-clone claim in the docs and the workflow while missing this
   third copy. Rewritten to say what is actually true — what changed is who holds the lock and
   when, not whether a close leads to compaction.

Gates green after all five: ruff, mypy 526 files, complexity ratchet unchanged, module-size
contract. Both tiers re-running before I re-push.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OPERATOR PROFILING (verbatim, live from another session):

"Confirmed: the compaction spawns a fresh git log --full-history child every few seconds
(7268 → 7496 …), each at ~100% CPU, holding the global write lock throughout. This is real but
pathologically slow progress on this large, long-history store."

## Confirmed against the code, and it is the SAME BUG CLASS AS 7084 — one scale up

`_compact_locked` builds the SNAPSHOT authorship ledger via
`_build_authorship_ledger` (`compact_txn.py:72`), which calls
`authorship.build_ticket_position_commit_map(ticket_dir)` (`attest/authorship.py:294`) —
ONE `git log --full-history` child PER TICKET, inside the store write lock. That is the
process the operator is watching spawn every few seconds.

The history here is worth stating, because it is the same defect recurring at the next scale:
- Bug 7084 / R1 found this as one full-history walk per SIGNED EVENT: measured 6.78s per event
  on a 71,041-commit branch, 47.5s of a 48.1s compact-on-close whose real mutation is ~0.4s.
- The fix batched it to per-TICKET: 0.53s for an 18-file ticket, 3.83s for a 159-file one.
- That was correct for compact-on-close, which folds ONE ticket. My work made `compact-all` the
  standing sweep, so the same call now runs once per ticket across the WHOLE store — and
  per-ticket becomes the new per-event. At ~0.5-4s each over thousands of tickets that is tens
  of minutes to hours of full-history walking, all of it lock-held.

So the operator's two fixes are exactly right, and I would add that fix 2's primitive ALREADY
EXISTS:

1. HOIST OUT OF THE LOCK. `git log` is read-only and never needed the write lock. Compute the
   ledger before acquiring; then lock → re-check the ticket's event set is unchanged → stage +
   commit → release. Identical discipline to the original P0 fix, applied one layer down.

2. AMORTIZE THE WALK — and do not write a new batcher for it.
   `authorship.build_introducing_commit_map()` (`attest/authorship.py:388`) already maps EVERY
   tracker event path to its introducing commit in a SINGLE walk: O(events + history), measured
   ~2s at real store scale, validated against the per-event resolver with 0 mismatches over 700
   sampled events, and it keeps `resolve_event_commit` as a fail-closed fallback for paths it
   misses. The sweep should build that map ONCE and query it per ticket, instead of N
   directory-scoped walks. ~2s total in place of hours.

Combined shape, as the operator put it: batch read-only prep (one walk, no lock), then short
per-ticket or small-batch lock windows for the mutations only. That also subsumes the chunking
fix — with the history walk gone from the critical section, the per-ticket lock window is just
the SNAPSHOT write, the renames and the commit, which is the ~0.4s the 7084 measurement already
attributed to real mutation.

Also still to fix in the same pass (from the earlier field report):
- `_commit_backfill`'s `git add -A` is unscoped and can commit a concurrent writer's in-flight
  event files under the compactor's message.
- `run_sweep`'s stand-aside probes `write_lock_is_busy` once before the loop, so a long sweep
  never re-yields to writers who arrive mid-run. It should re-probe between chunks.

Filing as a discovered_from ticket, NOT folding into 1733 — 1733 holds a clean LLM-Review +1
with zero findings and is blocked only on another session's `_config_schema.py` breach.

Corroboration, unintentionally: the `rebar comment` that posted the previous field-report note
waited 429s for the store write lock (holder pid 57999, held 77s and counting). The stall is
live and I am experiencing it while writing this up.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`choosy-arthrodic-barbet` removed compaction from the close path because it held the ONE store
write lock for up to 13m53s, starving concurrent agents. That landed the P0 fix but left the
store with NO standing compaction trigger: event logs grow until someone runs
`rebar compact <id>` by hand.

Two environments need covering, and only covering both is a fix. Where CI exists, a scheduled
sweep is the cheap amortized path. But **compaction must also work with no CI and no local
cron** — that is why the original design was linked to an operation. An adopter using rebar as
a library or CLI has neither, so a CI-only trigger leaves them with no compaction at all.

## Approach
Two triggers over ONE fold engine. Neither reintroduces the P0, because the P0 was that an
operation an agent WAITS ON held the lock; here nothing waited-on holds it.

**1. Make `compact-all` recur.** The sweep is nearly built: `compact_all_cli`
(`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:213`) already enumerates ticket dirs, honours
`--dry-run`/`--limit`/`--no-commit`, folds through `compact_cli`, batches one commit + push,
and reports counts. Its defect is SELECTION: `_scan_snapshot_state`
(`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:144`) picks only tickets lacking a `-SNAPSHOT.json`, so a
ticket folded once and since grown was never folded again — a one-time backfill, not a sweep.

Select on EITHER arm: (1) BACKFILL, preserved — no SNAPSHOT and at least one foldable event;
(2) RECURRENCE, new — foldable count over `compact.threshold`
(`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:81`), whatever the snapshot state. Arm 2 alone stops
backfilling small tickets; arm 1 alone is the one-time defect. Both converge: after a fold the
ticket has a SNAPSHOT and its live count is back under threshold.

FOLDABLE, not merely live, is load-bearing. The fold squashes only events older than the
horizon (`_compact_locked` partitions on `is_foldable`,
`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:365`; default 30 min, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:332`).
Selecting on raw live count would pick tickets whose excess events are all inside the horizon,
fold nothing, and pick them again forever. Selection reuses the fold's OWN predicate
(`src/rebar/_commands/_compact_policy.py`) against the same horizon, so the two cannot drift.

The driver must report honestly and cannot from the return code: `_compact_locked` returns 0
for a successful fold AND for all three no-op branches, so `if rc == 0: compacted += 1`
(`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:255`) counted them all as work. It observes the ARTIFACT
instead — the `*-SNAPSHOT.json` names before and after — counting a fold only when a new one
appeared.

**2. Scheduled sweep, where CI exists.** A 6-hourly workflow (`cron: '0 */6 * * *'`, also
`workflow_dispatch`) reusing `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`'s proven recipe: it
already runs a scheduled job that writes ticket events and pushes. Store mount
(`reconcile-bridge.yml:126-130`), bot identity (`:215-222`), and 0600
`REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` materialization (`:233-248`) are reused. No long-lived clone: each
run re-derives from `origin/tickets` on a disposable runner, so nothing accumulates. Env
identity needs no bootstrap — `_seam.env_id` (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:155`) reads
`<tracker>/.env-id`, which is content of the tickets branch.

**3. Operation-linked fallback — the floor that works everywhere.** On the close path, AFTER
the store lock is released and after the best-effort push, two O(1) checks: the just-written
ticket satisfies the two-arm selection (one listdir + parse of its own events, independent of
store size), OR a last-sweep stamp is older than a configured interval (one stat). The stamp
check is what makes it a real floor — without it a store whose closed tickets happen not to
need folding never folds the ones that do.

If either fires, spawn a DETACHED worker running the full sweep, reusing
`enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain`'s shape (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:252`) — the
PYTHONPATH bootstrap for the bare-python child, `_detach_kwargs()`, stdio to DEVNULL and a log
file. The session returns immediately; the worker's hold is the same as a manual
`rebar compact`, and never spans an LLM call.

One compactor at a time via a stamped advisory lock in `.rebar/`, using the same v2 stamp and
the same shared decision table `lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale` that
`enrich_drain._acquire_advisory_lock` (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:72`) uses, so
pid-recycle qualification, refusal-without-proof and the wall-clock ceiling are inherited.
Windows is a v1 no-op, mirroring the drain, because the store lock's fcntl import would crash a
detached child. A tri-state knob mirroring `overlap_drain` (async / always-inline for tests /
off) makes the fold synchronously testable and operator-disableable.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — two-arm selection, honest counting.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py` — new: the O(1) checks, stamped advisory lock, and
  detached spawn.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — call the trigger after the push.
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — the tri-state knob and the sweep interval.
- `.github/workflows/compact-sweep.yml` — the scheduled sweep.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — both triggers under I9b.
- `tests/unit/test_compact_all_selection.py`, `tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py`,
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_sweep_races.py` — new tests.

## Testing
- Selection: over-threshold-with-snapshot selected; excess-inside-horizon NOT selected;
  under-threshold-with-snapshot not; small snapshot-less still backfilled; both arms converge.
- Reporting: a fold that writes nothing is not counted; `--dry-run` and `--no-commit` never push;
  a sweep that folds nothing still pushes.
- Convergence: two clones fold one ticket, MERGE, and the merged store reduces identically.
- Trigger: fires on a foldable just-closed ticket; fires on a stale sweep stamp; does not fire
  when neither holds; does not spawn a second worker while the advisory lock is held; a stale
  advisory lock is reclaimed; `off` no-ops and `always` folds inline.
- The close itself still holds no lock across the trigger.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `compact-all` selects an already-snapshotted ticket whose FOLDABLE count exceeds the
      threshold, still backfills small snapshot-less tickets, and skips both under-threshold
      and all-inside-horizon tickets — asserted per case.
- [ ] Two consecutive sweeps converge: the second reports zero compacted.
- [ ] A fold that writes no SNAPSHOT is not counted as compacted; `--dry-run`/`--no-commit`
      never push; a sweep that folds nothing still pushes.
- [ ] Two concurrent folds from separate clones MERGE cleanly and the merged store reduces to
      the same events with none lost or duplicated.
- [ ] With no CI and no cron, closing a ticket triggers compaction out of band — a test asserts
      the detached worker is spawned (or, with the knob at `always`, the fold happens) and that
      the close itself holds the store lock across none of it.
- [ ] The trigger does not storm: with the stamped advisory lock held, no second worker is
      spawned; a provably-stale lock is reclaimed.
- [ ] The scheduled workflow exists with `cron: '0 */6 * * *'` and is `workflow_dispatch`-able;
      `docs/concurrency.md` documents both triggers; full local gate set and CI tiers pass.

file_impact.reason: two-arm foldable selection and honest artifact-based counting
new operation-linked fallback: O(1) checks, stamped advisory lock, detached worker spawn
invoke the trigger after the store lock is released and the push completes
tri-state trigger knob and the sweep interval
scheduled amortized sweep where CI exists
merge convergence and clone signing parity
